item.description: El Segundo, CA, - June 17, 2026: Los Angeles Chargers Defensive Coordinator Chris O'Leary speaks at a press conference during the team's minicamp at The Bolt training facility on Wednesday, June 17, 2026 in El Segundo, CA.(Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) Here’s a fun stat for you all this morning. Entering their bye week, the Chargers are tied for third in the NFL with 10 takeaways recorded by their defense. That’s behind only the Packers and Seahawks who are also tied with 11 on the year. The Broncos, Vikings, Steelers, and Raiders are the teams tied with the Chargers. Something you’ll most certainly notice here is that the Chargers are not like the others in this group. They’re winless, of course, and the only other winless team in the league (Dolphins) is way down near the bottom of the league. The teams surrounding the Chargers are 5-0, 4-3, and 3-3. If there’s anything to show just how lopsided the results have been for the Chargers defense compared to their offense, this is it. The numbers, for the most part, show that the Bolts should be at least 3-3 given this loose correlation. How incredibly frustrating. But good job Chris O’Leary! item.title: Rose salutes Bournemouth's past heroes ahead of AC Milan clash
item.description: Bournemouth coach Marco Rose (Glyn KIRK) Bournemouth manager Marco Rose paid tribute Wednesday to the team that helped preserve the club's English Football League status as they prepare to face Italian giants AC Milan in a landmark European fixture. The Cherries opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad and then won 3-0 at home to Sturm Graz last week. A match at home to AC Milan, one of Europe's leading clubs, was the last thing on Bournemouth fans' minds when the side were on the brink of dropping out of the Football League following a 17-point deduction ahead of the 2008/09 season as a result of failing to meet their terms for exiting administration. But Steve Fletcher's memorable goal against Grimsby eventually secured survival in Bournemouth's final home game of the season at Dean Court, which was followed by a mass pitch invasion after the final whistle by joyous Cherries fans. Rose only succeeded Andoni Iraola as Bournemouth boss before the start of this season but the German is well aware of a pivotal moment in the club's history as his side bid to maintain their perfect start to the Europa League. "We are looking forward to playing it, but I think many years ago the club had a much bigger game after the points reduction," Rose told a pre-match press conference. "They needed to win the last game at home and Fletch scored a goal –- but it is not about Fletch, it is about the whole team. This is a foundation to be here, to have these kind of games and we are looking forward to play this game. "It is a huge club of Europe which is coming here, but we feel prepared. We love to play this kind of games and now we are going to go for it." The Cherries beat Sunderland on Sunday for a first Premier League win under Rose. Now he wants to use that result as a springboard for continued success against an AC Milan side coached by former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim. "We feel in a good spot," added Rose. "As I said days ago, we had other topics, and now we won two games back to back and we are confident. "But even before the two games we won, I always told you that I feel confidence in my team. Now we have created a good momentum for us and we should use it." jdg/nf

item.title: Packers vs. Lions Week 7 TV Broadcast Map
item.description: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 27: Television camera operators for FOX Sports follow the action on the field during an NFL regular season Thanksgiving Day football game between the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions on November 27, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions meet up for their first of two 2026 regular season matchups on Sunday afternoon, nearly every media market in the United States will get to see the game on local television. These two teams have combined for five playoff appearances in the past three years, and both come into Week 7 with a winning record; as a result, FOX made it their late-afternoon game of the week when the NFL announced its schedule in May, and that slot has held up despite some early-season struggles on the Packers’ part. In fact, the Packers have bounced back remarkably from a 1-2 start that saw their game against the Chicago Bears two weeks ago — also initially slated for a large viewership in the 3:25 PM window — get flexed back into the early afternoon. (To be fair, the injury to Bears quarterback Caleb Williams surely factored in as well.) Green Bay now sits at 4-2 and on a three-game winning streak, while the Lions are 3-2 and coming off a bye week. These two teams have combined for some great games in the past few years, though 2025 saw the Packers sweep Detroit for the first time in Dan Campbell’s tenure as head coach of the Lions. Detroit is currently favored by 3 points, but this game very much feels like a tossup, especially if the Lions’ last-ranked passing defense continues to play the way it has to this point in the season. Ready to watch some fireworks? Good, because unless you’re in California and Nevada, you’re getting this game on your local FOX affiliate. The only other game on FOX in this time slot is Rams-Raiders, which will have a very limited local viewing area this week. Packers-Lions is shown in red on this week’s broadcast map below, provided by 506sports.com: As the top game on the network this week, Packers and Lions fans will get the network’s top broadcast tandem of Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady. Burkhardt has a day off from his duties as the pregame and postgame panel host for the World Series, but he’s not traveling far — games 1 and 2 will be held in Milwaukee on Friday and Saturday nights, giving him a short flight over Lake Michigan for Sunday’s game at Ford Field before he presumably makes a trip down to Tampa for Monday’s game 3.

item.description: ProShooter/Depositphotos Troy Aikman’s ESPN deal ends in 2027 Troy Kenneth Aikman works as an NFL analyst for ESPN after playing quarterback for the Dallas Cowboys. The former Cowboys quarterback had served as the network’s lead NFL analyst since 2017. For nine seasons, Romo worked with play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz on CBS’s leading NFL games. The company has not publicly named a permanent replacement for him beyond the current season. Mojahid_Mottakin/Depositphotos J.J. Watt holds the CBS role for 2026 J.J. item.title: Patriots vs. Bears series history ahead of Week 7
item.description: Following a game against their division rival Jets, the New England Patriots are up against a relatively unfamiliar opponent. They will travel to Chicago this week to take on the Bears on Thursday Night Football. It will be only the 17th meeting between the two storied franchises. Let’s take a look back at the most important moments from the first 16. Patriots vs. Bears series history Overall history: Even though the most memorable game of the series is a Bears win, it is the Patriots who have won the majority of the first 16 contests between the two organizations. New England holds an 11-5 edge after winning six of eight games since 2000. Those include a come-from-behind victory in 2002 that saw Tom Brady and company erase a 27-6 deficit in the late third quarter to ultimately win 33-30, as well as a lopsided 51-23 win during the 2014 season that was dominated by Rob Gronkowski and his three touchdowns. Chicago, as we will discuss shortly, is 1-0 against the Patriots in the playoffs. First game: Three years after the AFL-NFL merger, the Patriots and Bears met for the first time. The game at Soldier Field was a defensive affair that saw the two teams combine for only 98 net passing yards as well as six turnovers. Five of those were forced by New England, putting the team on the path to success. The winning points were scored in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Jim Plunkett found the end zone on a 5-yard quarterback keeper to give the Patriots a 13-10 win. Neither they nor the Bears were overly successful as a whole in 1973, though. | Highlights Most memorable game: Unfortunately for the Patriots, the most memorable out of their meetings with the Bears is Super Bowl XX. New England did manage to take a 3-0 lead and by doing so score the first points of the playoffs against Chicago’s famous 46 defense, but it ultimately was unable to hang on: the NFC champions scored 44 unanswered points, including the famous 1-yard rushing touchdown by defensive tackle William “Refrigerator” Perry in the third quarter. When all was said and done, the team of head coach Raymond Berry finished with just 123 net yards and turned the ball over six times en route to a 46-10 blowout that was the most lopsided defeat in a Super Bowl at the time. | Highlights Most recent game: The Patriots’ most recent matchup with the Bears brought more pleasant memories than the 1986 defeat, albeit at a smaller scale. Meeting at Soldier Field in 2024, the team led by then-head coach Jerod Mayo and then-rookie quarterback Drake Maye celebrated a 19-3 win. Maye was solid, but the defense was the story of the day: led by Deatrich Wise Jr. and Anfernee Jennings, who each registered two takedowns, the Patriots sacked Caleb Williams nine times and limited Chicago to 142 yards. | Highlights The Patriots and Bears will add to their series history on Thursday at 8:20 p.m. ET.

item.title: Where Jayson Tatum, Paul George Landed in Sporting News' NBA Opening Night Winners And Losers
item.description: Where Jayson Tatum, Paul George Landed in Sporting News' NBA Opening Night Winners And Losers originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Even in a loss, there was a lot to be encouraged about for the Celtics on opening night. Boston fell to Detroit, 121-113, allowing the Pistons to come back in the second half and spoil an excellent debut for newcomer Paul George. But from an optimistic stance, the new-look Celtics had a strong first half, looked impressive defensively and shot well from deep. For George and his co-star, Jayson Tatum, it was a fairly different start to the new season, though. Here's where Tatum and George were placed among the NBA's winners and losers from opening night by The Sporting News. MORE: NBA legend raises question about Jayson Tatum Jayson Tatum, Paul George Among NBA Opening Night Winners And Losers Even with the Celtics' blown 22-point lead to the Pistons, their new co-star, George was listed as a winner of the opening slate of games by Sporting News' Steph Noh. "George was the biggest bright spot," Noh wrote. "Boston was the perfect fit for George on paper, and he proved it in practice." George finished with 38 points, which set a new Celtics record for points in a team debut. He added five steals, flashing the two-way talent he was known for in the prime of his career. Tatum, meanwhile, was listed as a loser from the opening games. "The expectation was that he could fill into Brown's role from last year," Noh wrote of Tatum. "He did playmake for others, recording 11 assists on the day. His shot selection was mostly terrible though, and he was an ugly 6-of-23 from the field." With Tatum missing all seven of his 3-point attempts, it was a rough shooting night for him against Detroit. He'll be looking to bounce back as the season moves along — the best version of Tatum alongside a resurgent George could make the Celtics title contenders. Jayson Tatum in season debut: 13 PTS 11 AST 6-23 FG 0-7 3PT 2 PTS on 1-10 FG in the 2nd half. https://t.co/G5kDPxEvO0 — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) October 20, 2026 Meanwhile, a former Celtic, Jaylen Brown, was listed by Noh as a winner from opening night, as his new 76ers team beat the Knicks, 106-100. Brown, who scored 19 points, "had some good chemistry with LeBron," Noh wrote. There's a long way to go for both Brown and the 76ers, and Tatum, George and the Celtics in 2026-27. So far, it's looking like a potential win-win deal for Boston and Philadelphia. item.description: TORONTO, ONT - Jake Bauers of the Tampa Bay Rays looks on as he sits on the railing in the dugout during MLB game action against the Toronto Blue Jays at Rogers Centre on August 11, 2018 in Toronto, Canada. (Photo by Tom Szczerbowski/Getty Images) Getty Images Ozzie Timmons was the Milwaukee Brewers’ hitting coach for three seasons before returning to the Tampa Bay Rays in 2025 for a second stint on manager Kevin Cash’s staff. He had plenty of good things to say about Freddy Peralta the day the righthanded pitcher was acquired from the New York Mets at this season’s trade deadline. “He’s a great teammate, a competitor and he works hard,” said Timmons , who is Cash’s assistant hitting coach, a Tampa native, a former University of Tampa superstar and played in a dozen games for the Rays in 2000. “He’s a good person, a family man, has a lot of energy.” Peralta spent his first eight seasons in the majors with Milwaukee and was a two-time all-star, including 2025 when he won 17 games. In his short time with the Rays, Peralta been nothing less than sensational. That is especially the case since late August when he began a current stretch in which he is 7-0 with a 0.89 ERA in 10 appearances (nine starts) with the Rays winning all 10. Peralta, who won a pair of games and had an effective relief outing against Cleveland en route to winning ALCS MVP honors, and Timmons are among a number of connections between the Rays and Brewers. Timmons compared Peralta’s healthy clubhouse disposition to that of current Giants’ shortstop Willy Adames, who also played for both clubs and was a teammate of Peralta’s in Milwaukee. (More on Adames below.) Here are few more connections and similarities between the teams. Rays or Brewers will be first-time World Series winner Only five of 30 MLB teams have not won a World Series. The short list will whittle down to four with either the Rays, a 1998 expansion team, or the Brewers, who got their start as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 before moving to Milwaukee for the 1970 season, achieving a franchise first. The others who have yet to enjoy a late-October champagne soaking are the San Diego Padres (1969), Seattle Mariners (1977) and Colorado Rockies (1993). 1998 Expansion, Realignment To accommodate the expansion Tampa Bay Devils Rays’ residency in the American League East and that of fellow expansion partner, the Arizona Diamondbacks, in the National League West, some realignment was engineered to maintain an even number of teams in each league. With Tampa Bay on board, the Detroit Tigers shifted from the AL East to the AL Central. The Brewers moved from the AL Central to the NL Central to boost the National League’s inventory to 16 teams and keep the American League’s at 14. (The Astros moved from the NL Central to the AL West in 2013 to give each league 15 teams.) The above realignment made the World Series that will begin Friday night in Milwaukee possible. item.description: Football - NFL - Houston Texans v Jacksonville Jaguars - Wembley Stadium, London, Britain - October 18, 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen looks on Action Images via Reuters/Paul Childs | Action Images via Reuters Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. The Jacksonville Jaguars just can’t seem to get past the Houston Texans. The Jags have a 13-3 record in their last 16 regular season games, but two of those three losses came against the Texans, including Sunday’s 31-34 stunner . “That was not the result that you hunt up each week,” head coach Liam Coen said Monday. “You never want to lose, but I am glad that we’re able to respond in terms of the mental toughness of the group when it’s not perfect or everything’s not going exactly according to plan, and they just keep playing their tails off.” The Week 6 loss to Houston was a bummer, as was Jacksonville’s 10-point blown lead to Denver in Week 2. At the end of the day, though, the Jaguars have a 4-2 record going into their bye. They lead the AFC South by two games over the Texans (2-4), Indianapolis Colts (2-4), and Tennessee Titans (1-5). And it’s not fraudulent at all. The top four teams in point differential this year are the Jaguars (+50) and the three remaining undefeated teams: the San Francisco 49ers (+67), Kansas City Chiefs (+57), and Minnesota Vikings (+45). Jacksonville has performed like one of the best teams in the NFL — despite facing the league’s seventh-toughest schedule so far this season, per Sharp Football Analysis . They’re projected to have the single easiest schedule the rest of the way. “To be six weeks in and to feel confident that your team’s going to respond, that we’re made of the right stuff to respond, and we have so much football left that you’re excited about,” Coen said. “You’re excited about getting things corrected; you’re excited about being able to be in those moments again and maybe do it right or do it better the next time, as much as it hurts in the moment, in the aftermath. But I have a lot of confidence in this football team. Trevor [Lawrence] gives me so much confidence on a weekly basis as a play caller and the way that I think he’s seeing it right now and playing. I’m very excited about this football team.” Did the latest loss to Houston make you worried about Jacksonville’s lead in the division? item.title: Steve Young reveals HCs he’d most want to play for in today’s QB era
item.description: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Steve Young reveals HCs he’d most want to play for in today’s QB era appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Decades before the dual-threat quarterback became all the rage in the NFL, Steve Young was doing it regularly. Casually, even. He would have fit right in with today’s game with his perfect mix of accuracy, speed, and mobility. Young had a rocket arm, a sprinter’s legs, and a knack for turning broken plays into magical highlights. When he retired in 1999 after a 15-year career, he was a three-time champion, a two-time MVP, a six-time All-Pro, and a seven-time Pro Bowler. Young has kept tabs on the NFL , including the latest trends and modern strategies. On “The Pat McAfee Show,” he revealed the current coaches he would like to play for. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I’d run down the street to play for Kyle (Shanahan). If I could go to Sean McVay, Sean Payton, and Andy Reid, I’d sprint to them,” said Young. “Those are the guys. Those are innovators. Those were the guys who were innovating back when the rules changed in 2018. They innovated, and now that people caught up with them, you know what they did? They innovated again and again. That’s why I love them.” "I would run down the street to play for Kyle Shanahan.. I would sprint to play for Andy Reid, Sean McVay, and Sean Payton.. Those guys are the innovators" ~ @SteveYoungQB #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/DmAWd2kNto — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 20, 2026 The 65-year-old icon added that he could see himself excelling in today’s league , given his physical attributes and playing style. “It’s the era of the quarterback. It’s like you’ve given all the rules to make them feel the power to be great,” explained Young. “This is my game, man! I wanna game like this. This is how I wanna roll. Drop back, rip it, be efficient, beat a man, and just start running around, eating up yards. Oh, it’s a good game right now for quarterbacks.” "This is the era of the quarterback.. This is my game and I wanna be back out there.. Put me in coach" 😂😂 ~ @SteveYoungQB #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/b5OjyJbhxx — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 20, 2026 He starred for the Los Angeles Express, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the San Francisco 49ers, amassing a 94-49 record. Young would not need to reinvent his game to succeed in today’s NFL. If anything, modern schemes might make his job easier. After all, for the legendary quarterback, it does not really matter what era it is. item.title: Bills have another player suspended by NFL for a spitting incident vs. Raiders
item.description: Bills have another player suspended by NFL for a spitting incident vs. Raiders originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Buffalo Bills are coming off a big Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders and will now get a bye week to rest before returning to action in Week 8. But for that Week 8 matchup, the Bills are going to be without a key defensive back, and not due to injury. Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was suspended by the NFL for a spitting incident during the Bills vs. Raiders game. Somehow, he's not the only Bills DB to face this suspension from the NFL. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. is joining Gardner-Johnson on suspension for spitting in the Raiders game. A second Bills DB suspended for spitting incident vs. Raiders "Bills DB Sam Franklin Jr. was suspended one game today for unsportsmanlike conduct that the league said was a spitting incident vs. the Las Vegas Raiders," Schefter reports. Franklin and Gardner-Johnson are two defensive backs now set to be suspended for the Bills' Week 8 game coming out of their Week 7 bye. When the Bills face the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, they're going to be down a few defensive backs if these suspensions from the NFL hold up. MORE : Giants' QB plans get complicated after Jameis Winston collapse, J.J. McCarthy surge NFL Network's Mike Garafolo is reporting that Franklin "denies the allegation" that he spit toward or on someone during the Raiders game. Franklin will appeal the suspension and try to avoid missing Week 8's matchup. If both are out for that matchup, Buffalo will have to roll with Damar Hamlin, Jalon Kilgore, and Cole Bishop as their main safety rotation, as Gardner-Johnson and Franklin both might miss that game. It's a wild situation for the Bills to find themselves in, as two defensive backs are now suspended for Week 8, barring an appeal changing things. The Spanish giants contacted the defender in 2011 after he fractured his fibula against Tottenham, delivering a gesture that left a lasting impression on the Arsenal star. Sagna, who joined Arsenal under Arsene Wenger in 2007, had established himself as one of the Premier League’s most consistent right-backs before the injury interrupted his progress. The unexpected correspondence, signed by Real Madrid director Emilio Butragueño, gave him a reminder that his performances had attracted attention beyond English football. How Real Madrid surprised Sagna after his injury Sagna was enjoying the best football of his career when the injury struck. Having made more than 150 appearances for Arsenal by the end of the 2010/11 season, he suddenly faced an extended period away from the pitch. Recalling the circumstances surrounding the letter, Sagna explained how an unusual encounter at Arsenal’s training ground led to an unexpected moment of encouragement. “I broke my fibula against Tottenham in 2011. I was playing my best football, but unfortunately, I suffered that bad injury. “One day, right after that happened, I arrived at the training ground, and the receptionist was all flustered. She was looking left and right, all agitated, and whispering to me, “Come here, come with me, please.” Bacary Sagna recalls how a letter from Real Madrid helped him in his recovery. For Sagna, hearing from one of football’s biggest clubs while he was struggling with an injury offered reassurance that his performances were being recognised at the highest level. item.title: Kurt Warner shares Fernando Mendoza verdict after what he’s seen from Kirk Cousins
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images he Las Vegas Raiders have hit a real bump in the road, having lost their last three games, which is raising questions over their quarterback situation. First time head coach Klint Kubiak made veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins his starter ahead of the 2026 season. Through the opening three games, this looked like a masterstroke from Kubiak as the Raiders went unbeaten. However, the last three weeks have been a lot more difficult for the Raiders as they have gone 0-3 against the Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots and the Buffalo Bills. With the Raiders hitting a spot of turbulence, Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner has shared his verdict on potentially bringing Fernando Mendoza in as the starter. Kurt Warner urges Raiders not to make Fernando Mendoza their QB1 During the last three games, Cousins has failed to throw for more than two touchdowns in each game. Against the Patriots he was only able to throw for one touchdown. However, the veteran has not been a turnover machine like Sam Darnold with the Seattle Seahawks. “In my opinion, I don’t think they should as of yet. Again, I believe this team is not a great football team, but they’ve got some key pieces, including Kirk Cousins, that are making them competitive every time out. I just think it’s too early right now, with how competitive and how well Kirk is playing, to go to Fernando just yet,” Warner said on the Rich Eisen Show. “It may come a time when you feel like this team is not good enough and not going to make a playoff push, and you make that move. I just don’t think the time is right now. I think Kirk gives them confidence right now that, hey, even if we’re not winning these games, we’re competitive every single time out. I think that is really important for that organisation right now.” Next up for the Raiders is a game against the Los Angeles Rams which could provide them with a big opportunity to get their season back on track. The Rams lost again at the weekend against the Arizona Cardinals as their season continues to derail. Top spot in the AFC West certainly looks a tough task for the Raiders, but they are still only one win behind the Denver Broncos, who have also looked far from convincing this season. Until the chances of a spot in the postseason is off the cards, Cousins feels like the way forward for Vegas. item.description: The rest of this conference needs to thank BYU. Maybe send them flowers. Or a box of Crumbl cookies. By beating Notre Dame in Week 7 of college football , BYU legitimized the entire Big 12. The league has never sent two teams to the CFP and hasn’t won a CFP game in the 12-team era. They were trending towards being CFP afterthoughts again this season after a non-conference slate that just repeatedly saw Big 12 teams lose to Big Ten and SEC foes. But now they have a marquee win they can point to and say this conference can compete with the “blue bloods” of college football. item.title: ‘Don’t do this’ – Shannon Sharpe hammers the NFL after what they’ve said about Jalen Hurts
item.description: Photo by Kevin Mazur/Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Fanatics The Jalen Hurts health scare story has gripped the NFL with serious concerns being raised about the players’ welfare being shown by teams. The Philadelphia Eagles’ quarterback will not play again this season after it was discovered that he had blood clots in his lungs. How the diagnosis came about is what has really frustrated people around the league. Hurts was allowed to fly to and from London despite there being an undiagnosed issue. That issue turned out to be blood clots which has now seen the quarterback forced to miss the remainder of the season. Given the severity of the health scare, the NFL addressed the protocols taken by the Eagles’ staff in a recent meeting with the media. However, Shannon Sharpe has been left furious with some of their answers. Shannon Sharpe criticises NFL over Jalen Hurts assessment The NFL has come to the conclusion that the Eagles did not violate the injury report policy and will, therefore, not be fined for allowing Hurts to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. “I love the NFL… but I hate when they do this. Don’t do this,” Sharpe said on the Nightcap show. “If I’m not mistaken, the way I read it is that you wait till you get to London to do the MRI, and then you’re like, ‘Oh, okay.’ Tell me the professional says that you should be flying even with a superficial blood clot. Wouldn’t you think you would let him clear that up? Because knowing that it could travel to your lungs, it could travel to your heart. “They know they’re under [pressure].” Questions are going to be asked as the weeks go on as to why Hurts was allowed to travel and play in the London game despite the NFL’s conclusion as Nick Sirianni passed on a number of opportunities to comment on the situation earlier in the week. It is clear to see that former NFL stars like Sharpe have not been impressed with what they have seen unfold over the last few days. item.title: Vincent Kompany expected back on Bayern Munich touchline in time for Arsenal clash
item.description: Vincent Kompany expected back on Bayern Munich touchline in time for Arsenal clash Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany is now expected to take his place on the touchline for Wednesday evening’s Champions League encounter against Arsenal after returning to team preparations following a viral infection. According to reports from Kicker , Sport Bild and Sky Germany , the Belgian participated in Wednesday morning’s activation session before accompanying the squad to their team hotel. The 45-minute session took place behind closed doors at Bayern’s Säbener Straße training facility. Sport Bild subsequently reported that the 40-year-old traveled with his players to the team’s hotel in Unterschleißheim, where Bayern were scheduled to complete their final preparations for the clash with Mikel Arteta’s side. Sky Germany also filmed Kompany arriving at the hotel, providing further confirmation of his return to the squad’s preparations. Although Bayern have not officially confirmed whether Kompany will coach from the touchline, the latest developments strongly suggest that he will be available against Arsenal. Kompany’s availability remained uncertain on Tuesday The news represents a significant improvement on the situation just 24 hours earlier. Kompany missed Tuesday’s final training session and pre-match press conference while recovering from a viral infection that had also affected him during Saturday’s 6-1 Bundesliga victory over RB Leipzig . Assistant coach Aaron Danks, who had assumed responsibility for preparations in Kompany’s absence, expressed uncertainty about whether the Belgian would recover in time . “Getting Vincent to rest is a difficult challenge,” Danks told reporters at Tuesday’s pre-match press conference. “He’s at home resting. We take it day by day, so I’m unsure of his involvement tomorrow.” Kompany’s illness had reportedly been accompanied by discomfort affecting his legs and hips, limiting his mobility during the Leipzig match. The Bayern trainer spent much of that encounter seated, leaving Danks and the remaining coaching staff to issue instructions from the touchline. Wednesday’s developments nevertheless indicate that Kompany has recovered sufficiently to resume his preparations with the team. Bayern will still be without Joshua Kimmich, who is unavailable following a bereavement in his immediate family . Michael Olise remains suspended, while Jamal Musiala is sidelined through injury. Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer, meanwhile, is expected to return after overcoming the foot problem that kept him out of Bayern’s previous two matches. The German record champions welcome Arsenal to the Allianz Arena at 21:00 CEST, with both clubs hoping to strengthen their positions in the Champions League league phase. GGFN | Peter Weis

item.title: Bournemouth receive major Junior Kroupi injury boost ahead of Man Utd clash
item.description: Bournemouth receive major Junior Kroupi injury boost ahead of Man Utd clash Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi has returned to first-team training and could make his long-awaited comeback against Manchester United this weekend. The 20-year-old has been sidelined since July after suffering a fractured metatarsal during the club’s pre-season training camp in Austria. However, Sky Sports reporter Mark McAdam has revealed that Kroupi is back training with his teammates and could feature in Sunday’s Premier League encounter at Old Trafford. Bournemouth manager Marco Rose has also confirmed the Frenchman’s progress, raising hopes that he could make his first appearance of the campaign. “Junior is back into the team training, but not on the UEFA list,” Rose explained . “But maybe we can have him for some minutes in Manchester.” Kroupi will therefore remain unavailable for Thursday’s Europa League meeting with AC Milan, having been omitted from Bournemouth’s European squad during his recovery. Nevertheless, his return to full training represents a significant development after initial concerns that he could remain sidelined until November. The France Under-21 international underwent surgery in late July after sustaining the injury while taking a shot during a training session. He subsequently spent several weeks rehabilitating before resuming individual work on the grass earlier this month. Reports from France previously indicated that Kroupi had targeted the Manchester United fixture for his return, although Bournemouth were determined not to rush his recovery. His latest progress suggests that the club could now be ready to reintegrate him gradually into competitive action. Kroupi established himself as one of the Premier League’s most promising young forwards during an impressive debut campaign in England. The former Lorient attacker scored 13 league goals last season, becoming Bournemouth’s leading scorer and attracting interest from several major European clubs. His performances also saw him break the record for most Premier League goals by a teenager in their debut season. Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur and Barcelona were among the clubs linked with the youngster before his injury effectively ended speculation surrounding a summer departure. Bournemouth subsequently maintained that Kroupi was not available for transfer, with the forward remaining an important part of their long-term plans. Rose has relied on other attacking options during his absence, including Evanilson and summer signing Alvaro Rodriguez. However, Kroupi’s potential return would provide another goalscoring option as Bournemouth balance domestic commitments with their first European campaign. The Cherries visit Manchester United on Sunday, with Kroupi now hoping to earn his first competitive minutes since recovering from surgery.

Just starting physically — they are of similar size (Durzi is 6-foot, 199 pounds; Trocheck 5-foot-11, 187 pounds) with dark hair, and quick smile — dare we say mischievous smirk. Heck, each player has a pretty prominent nose that’s clearly taken a knock or two over the years. Personality-wise, Durzi and Trocheck are both very outgoing, comfortable with the media, funny, honest, and extremely popular with their teammates. On the ice, even though Durzi is a defenseman and Trocheck a forward, they both bring a strong commitment to playing a diligent two-way game. Each is a right-shot and trusted in all game situations at even strength, as well as on the power play and penalty kill. And neither is to be f***ed with, even if they’re far from being the biggest players on the ice. They even make similar salaries. item.description: Tracy Morgan delivered an unexpected shot at Bronny James during the New York Knicks ‘ championship celebration on Tuesday night. The comedian and longtime Knicks superfan criticized the Los Angeles Lakers guard during NBC Sports’ pregame coverage at Madison Square Garden. “Bronny look like he got JUCO ball written all over him,” Morgan said. “I just want to say what I feel. What you want?” The remark caught the broadcast panel off guard, with former Knicks star Carmelo Anthony laughing beside Morgan. The moment soon circulated across social media, drawing mixed reactions from the basketball community. item.title: Dana White & UFC producing Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury claims once again dismissed
item.description: Dana White & UFC producing Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury claims once again dismissed appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After months of waiting around and seeing rumors emerge, Netflix has now confirmed the much-awaited Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury fight for later this year. The fight is now set to take place on Dec. 11, 2026, at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. A few weeks ago, UFC president Dana White claimed to have a significant role in promoting and producing the Fury vs. Joshua fight. However, Matchroom Boxing’s Eddie Hearn publicly disagreed with White’s alleged involvement. This soon followed a back-and-forth banter between the two , with the Misfits Boxing co-founder also suggesting a match between the two. While White insists on his involvement in the fight , Hearn continues to claim that the UFC President is contractually barred from having any involvement in the Joshua vs. Fury boxing match. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Eddie Hearn has been Joshua’s promoter since he made his professional debut in 2013. Joshua’s contract for his fight with Fury is believed to specifically state that Dana White cannot be involved in the event. “Under our contract, he can’t. So that’s really where we stand on it. Sela has confirmed to us in writing that Dana White and the UFC are not doing the production for this show. So, we have to go through the same process, blah blah blah. “We will speak to Netflix and guess what? Whisper, the production company that did the production for Fury/Makhmudov, they have a contract to do the production for Fury vs. AJ on Netflix,” Hearn said while speaking on iFL TV on YouTube. Hearn finished by claiming that if White and the UFC want to speak with him regarding changing the contract about the production, he is open to a conversation. Despite the disagreements, the fight is still on for Dec. 2026. item.title: German triathlon boss to run for DOSB presidency
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Prof. Dr. Martin Engelhardt attends a general assembly of the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB). Engelhardt is a DOSB vice president and will run for the presidency. (is associated with: «German triathlon boss to run for DOSB presidency») Laszlo Pinter/dpa German Triathlon Union (DTU) chief Martin Engelhardt will run again for the presidency of the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB), it was announced on Wednesday. The DTU has submitted the election proposal together with other DOSB member federations for Engelhardt to run against Michael Mronz, a member of the International Committee (IOC) who was proposed by a selection committee of German sport. Mronz has good Olympic connections through his IOC role which could help Munich's bid for the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Games. The DOSB president is elected on December 5 at its assembly and will succeed Thomas Weikert, who is not seeking another term. Engelhardt is making a second attempt for the DOSB presidency. He lost in 2018 against Alfons Hörmann. Engelhardt said he would be fully available from April 2027 after ending his profession as head physician at an Osnabrück hospital. He was DTU president 1987-2001 and again since 2011, is a DOSB vice president and was a doctor on the 2004 and 2008 German Olympic teams. “I know the sport inside out, from club level right up to the world governing body, through research into high-performance sport and from having been at two Olympic Games alongside our athletes,” Engelhardt said. “I would like to put forward a proposal to the German sporting community that reflects its diversity: a sports strategy for Germany, which we will implement in collaboration with politicians, with the aim of tackling major national and international challenges in a united and successful manner."

item.title: FIA introduces strict rules to prevent ‘tricks’ within the cost cap regulations
item.description: The FIA is significantly tightening the rules for Formula 1 teams from 2027 onwards. The motorsport federation wants to prevent teams from gaining an advantage through other projects within their organisations that fall outside the cost cap. The measures go so far that they could even affect where employees are allowed to work. The cost cap limits how much teams can spend on their Formula 1 operations. Its purpose is to prevent the wealthiest teams from investing unlimited funds in their performance. Enforcement becomes more complicated, however, when an organisation has departments working on other technologies alongside its F1 team. Red Bull, for example, has its ‘Advanced Technologies’ division, Mercedes has ‘Applied Science’, and Aston Martin has ‘Performance Technologies’. Ferrari is also working on the Hypersail sailing project. These activities are separate from Formula 1, but the technical expertise they develop could also be of interest to the racing departments. That is the FIA’s concern. An employee could officially be working on a project outside Formula 1 while their expertise also benefits the F1 team. The associated costs would then remain outside the cost cap, even as the team benefits from their work. However, there is no proof that teams have actually broken the rules in this way. F1 staff must work separately The FIA has previously introduced measures to prevent such arrangements. For example, technical expertise transferred to the F1 team from another department had to be counted towards the cost cap. It was also stipulated that the full salaries of employees contributing to F1 activities must fall within the spending limit. From 2027, the governing body is going a step further. A new 12-page chapter in the operational regulations requires a strict separation between the F1 department and employees working on other projects. The FIA has significantly tightened a number of rules - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool The FIA has significantly tightened a number of rules - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool This means, among other things, that the two groups will no longer be allowed to work in the same office. Factories must be divided into restricted-access zones with electronic entry controls. Teams must retain access logs for three years so the FIA can later check who entered which areas. Facilities such as wind tunnels, simulators and engine test benches may still be used by both departments under certain conditions. However, employees from the two groups may not be present at the same time, and no information may be exchanged. Restrictions will also apply to shared spaces. The reverse route is also being closed off: information from those other projects may not flow to the F1 team. The FIA wants to prevent an organisation from conducting research outside the cost cap and then using the results to make its Formula 1 car faster. Formula 1 teams face further restrictions related to the budget cap - Photo: Red Bull Contentpool Formula 1 teams face further restrictions related to the budget cap - Photo: Red Bull Contentpool Moving between departments within the same company will become harder The transfer of employees between departments will also be restricted. They must then commit contractually to working exclusively on F1-related matters for at least 12 months. Strict conditions will apply to moves in the opposite direction as well. An F1 employee moving to another technical department must receive a new contract, revised access rights and a new email address. That employee must then work exclusively for the new department for 12 months. Their salary will also continue to count towards the F1 cost cap for that year. This means a team cannot simply move staff to another department during the season to free up cap space.

(Photo by Borja B. Hojas/Getty Images) | Getty Images The game of college basketball requires more in 2026 than it did 20 years ago. In the past, head coaches brought in groups of freshmen to build out a mini dynasty over four years. Some years would be lighter than others to ensure playing time, development and maintaining a winning culture. Today, with the ability to transfer there are multiple ways to build out a team each year. Some programs build out new teams basically each season. For Ohio State women’s basketball, who returned eight of their 11 players from last season, and four of five starters, this would be considered a light recruiting year. The transfer portal did not yield any results for head coach Kevin McGuff and the program landed three freshmen in a program that does not usually rely heavily on younger players. Of those three freshmen, one has already stood out to not only those that recruited her but everyone who steps onto the court alongside her. Adriana Díaz is a Spanish international who enters Ohio State ready to make an impact on day one. In August, Díaz was with the Spanish youth national team at the U18 Eurobasket Championship for her second year in a row. Much like 2025, Spain rolled through competition to win its seventh gold medal at the U18 level. Part of that was the play of Díaz. The big averaged 19.9 minutes per game. In that time, Díaz averaged 8.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game. In the quarter-finals against Italy, Díaz had 10 points, 6 rebounds, 3 steals and 2 assists and an astounding +43 +/-, which means that when she was on the court, Spain outscored Italy by 43 points. What to Expect Watch an Ohio State women’s basketball game and the predominant strategy is to play strong defense, force turnovers and turn those turnovers into easy points. That’s in the full court. Once the Buckeyes get to the half court, movement and leaving space under the basket helps let players like point guard Jaloni Cambridge find space and make plays. That includes sometimes parking outside of the arc, running to the basket and dishing out for three-point opportunities. Díaz can do all of that. The steals. The speed in transition. The running to the basket. The passing. The shooting from beyond the arc. All of it. “You gonna have to play this video back in four years, but no one’s seen it yet. But AD [Díaz], she’s going to be one of the best Buckeyes to ever come out of here,” Kennedy Cambridge told reporters. “She came in first day, I literally looked at her and was like, ‘Yeah, we’re gonna be great.’ Man, like, but also, with her being bigger, she can guard, she can shoot. She’s so strong too, y’all. I really don’t even understand.“ “I took a charge on her, and I’ll never do that again,” Jaloni Cambridge added. When people reference a European big, they think of somebody who has an all-around game. Someone who can use their strength inside and also hit midrange baskets or deep shots. Díaz fits that definition and she can also go to the basket without the sometimes awkwardness that comes with size for a college basketball player. At 6-foot-1, Díaz will not be inch for inch as big as some of the post players in the conference, and even her own locker room, but that slightly smaller size gives the freshman the ability to attack the basket like a Jaloni Cambridge. Díaz can get inside with speed, take on one or two defenders and push defenders back or hit shots from the outside. “She’s got our offense immediately, our defense immediately,” Elsa Lemmilä told reporters. “We barely have to coach her because she’s doing so well.” Prediction Normally, being a freshman in McGuff’s system means a lot of learning from the bench. Díaz will have a lot more learning on the court. In previous years, McGuff mentioned how international play separates new college players from those who played high school basketball and AAU alone. On a Spanish team that features a wealth of Power Four recruits, like UCLA freshman Somto Okafor and Houston point guard Marta Llompart. So, Díaz played alongside college-level talent. UCLA earned two commitments from that Spanish youth team with 6’5 center Anna Smykovskaia set to join the Bruins for the 27-28 season. All of that to say that Díaz is college basketball ready. It will be no surprise to see Díaz come in to relieve Kylee Kitts or Elsa Lemmilä inside the post, because Díaz can play both roles. Should either of the two bigs miss time due to injury, Díaz can move into the starting lineup. A 20-minute average per game is not out of the question and that is possibly a low estimate if what Díaz’s new teammates say translates onto a college court. Ohio State’s depth does not have a lot of experience. Only Ella Hobbs and Seini Henry are upperclassmen and neither Buckeye started a game yet in their third seasons with the program. There is a strong argument to be made that Díaz is the most experienced player on that bench for McGuff to bring into games, and he will. Even so, expect a learning curve because Díaz will play some of the best players in the country. Also, teams will begin to figure out her game too. Still, the future looks bright for Díaz in her first season. Highlights Below shows how Díaz fit into the Ohio State system so quickly. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could really use a shot in the arm. Tampa only has one win on the season after missing Baker Mayfield in their last few games. The latest injury update on Tampa’s franchise quarterback makes it perfectly clear what he needs to do before returning to the field. NFL insider Ian Rapoport gave another injury update on Mayfield leading up to Week 7. The veteran quarterback’s availability this week all depends on one displaying one simple skill in practice. “Baker Mayfield, the Bucs quarterback, is expected to be on the practice field. He has missed three weeks, he’s dealing with a dislocated thumb,” Rapoport said on Tuesday via NFL Live. “It is a very simple thing: can he grip the ball and throw it? If he can, he is expected to play. If he cannot, it’ll be another week of Jalon Daniels in Tampa.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mayfield has already missed three games this season with this thumb injury. Fortunately, the rookie Daniels has played well in relief of Mayfield. In fact, Tampa’s only win on the season came at the hands of their undrafted rookie. Earlier this week, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles seemed to hint that Daniels could remain the starter in Week 7. “(Todd) Bowles said Wednesday will be important for evaluating Baker Mayfield and his thumb but they’ll plan as if Jalon Daniels is starting again in terms of initial game-planning,” Greg Auman of FOX Sports reported on Monday. Tampa may only be 1-5 on the season, but they are still only a few games back in the NFC South standings. That means they could feel pressure to get Mayfield back quickly to help save their season. Especially with a crucial divisional showdown coming up this weekend. Next up for the Buccaneers is a road game against the Panthers. This NFC South contest kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Oct. 25 from Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte. item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
